verified: Teacher-forced decision-test numbers are contaminated by the recorded future controls. On the 105 f105 decision windows (33 stuck within 8 s, 73 infeasible runs; artifacts/traverse/wp7_stall_diag/decision_verdict.json) a single scalar of the recorded future controls, mean |delta-throttle| over the next 8 s, ranks 'stuck within 8 s' at AUC 0.96 (my recomputation from wp7_cache_v1 act arrays, recorded frames only; verifier: sensitivity 0.79 at 5 % FPR, 0.93 from the first 2 s, 0.92/0.61 with the harness's end-of-recording padding), above every teacher-forced model (best 0.90 in wp8_eval_summary/verdict_decision.txt). Throttle level at t0-1 is uninformative (AUC 0.51, mine). The future brake fraction gives 0.96 for run infeasibility (verifier).

The decision windows are not a foresight benchmark: |steering| at the last context frame (t0-1), a scalar from the context that is Chrono's own controller reacting to a stall already under way, ranks the label at AUC 0.84 pooled, 0.82 en route, 0.75 at rest (mine; mean |steer| 0.49 on stuck vs 0.18 on passing windows), higher than every tracker-in-the-loop model (0.50-0.76) and than the cheap context-only classifier (0.71). Holding that recorded control constant into the imagination ('hold', no future pattern) gives progress-AUC 0.85/0.87/0.92/0.94 for frozen/p6/ar03/mom_s1, and replacing the held steering by route-following steering drops it to 0.65/0.83/0.71/0.83 (/tmp/decision_ctrl.log, /tmp/decision_ctrl2.log).

Rest/en-route stratification: 41 windows are decided from the first 16 frames (26 stuck, all launch failures; 15 that launch and fail later, so every rest window is an infeasible run) and 64 en route (7 stuck / 57). The at-rest flag alone scores 0.79 and -vx at t0-1 0.82 pooled but only 0.57 en route / 0.66 at rest (mine and verifier). This inflates the teacher-forced scores (+0.05 to +0.12), the scalars (+0.21) and the cheap classifier's local AUC, but NOT the tracker-in-the-loop scores (pooled minus within-stratum -0.08 to +0.07) and not the cheap classifier's 0.84 for run infeasibility, which is an en-route-only number (0.83) because the rest stratum has no feasible run (verifier). Within strata the tracker-in-the-loop gives en route 0.61-0.77, rest 0.40-0.70, with 7 en-route positives (95 % intervals roughly 0.45-0.95).

The pure-pursuit 'below chance' reading of notes 13.10 is a launch-stratum effect, not the constant-throttle cue: pooled 0.32/0.43 for p6/ar03 is 0.81/0.77 en route and 0.15/0.30 at rest (verifier); adding tracker-matched AR(1) throttle noise to pure pursuit leaves it at 0.33/0.42/0.42 for p6/ar03/mom_s1 (/tmp/decision_ctrl.log, mode pp_ar, mean |dthr| 0.027-0.032). At rest pure pursuit commands 0.75-1.0 throttle (pure_pursuit_actions in src/nedm/traverse/tracker_env.py) and the stall-trained models launch a perched vehicle under it.

Harness artefact in cmd_decision (scripts/traverse_wp7_stall_diagnosis.py lines 827-846): prog_end freezes when a rollout terminates at the route end but prog_1s is read from the live progress buffer, so disp_last1s is meaningless for runs that finish inside 8 s and pred_stuck fires on them. My count from decision_verdict.json: 25 of 32 feasible windows flagged stuck with the tracker for the frozen model, 26 of 32 for wp8d_ar03 (e.g. x_crater7_h270 direct_v5: progress 27.0 = route end, disp_last1s -0.50, vx_end 3.23, pred_stuck True). The 'pred stuck (stuck/pass)', 'outcome accuracy per candidate' and 'gate [tracker] x/5' rows of decision_*.log and verdict_decision.txt are therefore not interpretable; the AUCs by -progress are unaffected.

Tracker-in-the-loop model differences are inside noise: layout-cluster bootstrap k120 0.50 [0.35,0.71], frozen 0.65 [0.37,0.89], ar03 0.71 [0.49,0.84]; paired k120-frozen -0.14 [-0.43,+0.13], ar03-frozen +0.05 [-0.12,+0.24] (signal analyst, 33 layouts). Moving the decision point does not help: with the WP3 tracker the AUC is 0.62/0.66/0.66/0.64 at 2 m lead, 0.65/0.71/0.71/0.69 at 5 m and 0.67/0.72/0.76/0.75 at 10 m for frozen/p6/ar03/mom_s1 (/tmp/plan32/decision_lead{2,10}.log, verdict_decision.txt; I read the logs), sensitivity 0.18-0.44 at 5 % FPR.

Route-level yardstick (closed-loop imagination from rest with the WP3 tracker over the whole route, f105, 151 stop+launch vs 451 feasible, score = imagined time, rejected = 60 s): frozen AUC 0.686 (layout bootstrap [0.56,0.80]) -> wp8e_mom_only 0.775, wp8_p3_k80 0.774, wp8_p6_k80_prog 0.759, wp8e_mom_s1 0.758, wp8d_ar03 0.742, wp8e_mom_k120 0.685 (analyst and verifier recomputed from wp8_eval/<run>/imagine_f105/rows.json). Paired differences exclude zero only for the post-hoc best of 62 runs (P 0.01-0.02) and are borderline for the pre-registered primary and its seeds (P 0.06-0.10). Commanded speed alone gives 0.55-0.58 and the separation survives stratifying by commanded speed (0.74-0.78). The gain comes from rejecting more routes (58 -> 150-240) plus imagined-time ordering; the stall-vs-feasible rejection odds ratio stays at the frozen level (4.8; median 4.5 over 62 runs); P(stall|accepted) 0.18 -> 0.12-0.17. The point metrics correlate with the route AUC only through rejection volume (partial Spearman -0.04 to +0.07) and with the pick at about zero (-0.03/+0.01/+0.05); the pick spans 31-43 of 52 (sd 2.6) and correlates with neither AUC.

Teacher-forced headline fractions reproduce exactly (k120 0.35/0.52/0.42, AR 0.43/0.63/0.42; ar03 0.43/0.48/0.33) on one arena with strong clustering (46 stops on 26 layouts, 105 launch failures on 15). Paired layout-cluster bootstrap vs frozen: 'stop predicted' +0.02 to +0.20, none excluding zero (ar03 +0.20 [-0.02,+0.40] borderline); 'hold' +0.22 to +0.33 and 'launch' for k120/mom_only/mom +0.19 to +0.23 clear zero; CI half-widths about 0.2 are a power statement (verifier). Stall aborts are called at 0.09-0.30 (frozen 0.17) vs stationary timeouts 0.39-0.57 (0.30); with the tracker generating the controls the gain shrinks to 0.13-0.28 vs 0.17.

Training positives are thin and every augmented run's best checkpoint is its first: train_log.jsonl shows the validation stall score minimal at step 1000 and rising thereafter (wp8d_ar03 1.07 -> 1.23, wp8e_mom_k120 1.04 -> 1.28, wp8e_mom 1.36 -> 1.51, wp8e_mom_s1 1.22 -> 1.48, wp8e_mom_only 1.23 -> 1.56; val one-step loss +10-15 %; mine). f101-f104 hold 100 true stops / 63 launch failures / 202 momentum events against f105's 46 / 105 / 99 (events.json, analyst).

Design (a) prior: the cheap terrain-profile predictor gives AUC 0.766 for infeasibility on f105 (wp7_cheap_true/readout.json; 0.78 sealed); imagined time alone 0.64-0.72 (imagine_f105/summary.json); a 5-fold-by-layout MLP on the imagined summary features gives 0.58/0.60/0.65/0.67/0.77 at seed 0 and 0.59/0.60/0.63/0.62/0.73 (+/-0.02-0.06) over five seeds for frozen/ft_mix/p6/ar03/mom_s1 (verifier re-ran /tmp/plan32/head_floor.py). The from-rest imagined mean speed separates the 46 true stops from 133 matched passes at 0.78 (frozen) to 0.83-0.89 (stall-trained), commanded speed alone 0.71, residual beyond it 0.46 frozen / 0.61-0.69 stall-trained (verifier). Plan §32's 'cheap classifier 0.84' reads the TRUE recorded state 5 m before the stop, of which commanded speed gives 0.725 and its local-stuck sensitivity is 0.00 at 5 % FPR — it is not evidence for a from-rest imagined-state head.

No gate has headroom on the existing arenas: the fastest-commanded-speed heuristic fails on 4/1/1/5/8 layouts of f101-f105 (19 of 222; 10 contact-only) and 7/93 sealed (3 contact-only, notes 13.5); on f105 its 8 failures are 4 contact-only, 2 stalls, 2 timeouts (my re-run of /tmp/plan32/ceiling.py over wp7_cache_v1/labels.json). A matched-rate random rejecter scores 43.9 +/- 0.7 against the heuristic's 44 (audit_workflow_result.json); the cheap predictor as gate+fastest gives 45/52 (tau 0.5) and 46/52 (tau 0.3) on f105 and 85/93 sealed (0 fixes, 1 break) vs 86 (verifier). The sealed arenas have been looked at three times and notes 13.5 says they must not be used again.

Design (c) has no signal to act on: every in-imagination controller either exploits the model (tracker retrained inside wp8d_ar03: AUC 0.33, pick 26-30/52; decision_wp8_tracker_ar03_s*.log) or scores 0.62-0.76 at 2/5/10 m lead; only 5 f105 layouts have a decision at the decision point and the fastest candidate passes all 5 (regret 1.06); one 1 m/s speed step separates stall from pass on 48 of 65 momentum layouts (notes 12.1), so a model-free 'add throttle when slowing' rule would take the credit.

Replaying the frozen imagination's tracker actions open-loop into the stall-aware models gives 0.64/0.67/0.65 (p6/ar03/mom_s1), at or below the tracker's 0.71/0.71/0.69 (/tmp/decision_ctrl.log mode frozen_ol). Ensemble disagreement across the 10 stored tracker-driven closed-loop runs (frozen, ft_mix, p6, p6_s2, p9, ar03, mom, mom_k120, mom_only, mom_s1 from decision_verdict.json + decision_f105_v2.json; decision_pp.json stores pure-pursuit rows under the same 'pol' key and must be excluded): std of imagined end speed AUC 0.78 (layout bootstrap [0.58,0.88]; en route 0.74, rest 0.61; run infeasibility 0.86; sensitivity 0.36) and std of progress 0.80 [0.61,0.89], versus the analyst's 0.80/0.79/0.70/0.85/0.55 — same size, chosen post hoc among aggregators (mean end speed 0.42, min 0.79), never run sealed.
corrected: 'The teacher-forced AUC is essentially all future-control leak' holds only for the fingerprint model wp8_p6_k80_prog (0.89 -> 0.48 with no future controls: route-following steering + context-mean throttle + tracker-matched AR(1) noise). The augmented models keep 0.71 (wp8d_ar03) and 0.78 (wp8e_mom_s1) under the same probe (frozen 0.64), i.e. 60-77 % of their above-chance teacher-forced discrimination, at or above their tracker-in-the-loop numbers (verifier's /tmp/refute_ctrl.py). The donor-swap correlations (0.94-0.98 vs 0.76-0.86) appear for the frozen model too (0.98 vs 0.86-0.89) and so do not isolate a leak; the label-discordant subset is n=4 / n=9 and physically ambiguous on the same-rest-pose launch layout. The recorded steering costs the stall-trained models at most 0.05 AUC (route-following steering + recorded throttle: 0.89/0.81/0.82) and 0.19 for the frozen model; of the 13/21/12/15 stuck windows 'imagined moving with < 3 m progress', 8/12/8/11 roll backwards on the route and only 4/1/3/3 leave it.

'The pooled AUC is inflated for every predictor' overreaches: the tracker-in-the-loop scores, on which 13.10-13.11 rest, are not inflated (frozen -0.02, p6 +0.03, ar03 +0.07, k120 -0.07, and en route is at or above pooled in 7 of 9 models), and the cheap classifier's 0.84 for run infeasibility is entirely en route. The stratified comparison offered as evidence ('-vx 0.82 above the classifier 0.71/0.84') is itself the pooled artefact: within strata the classifier beats the scalar (0.73 vs 0.57 local en route, 0.83 vs 0.78 infeasibility en route). The headline conclusions of 13.7 survive stratification (teacher-forced 0.88/0.82 vs cheap 0.78/0.36; collapse with the tracker to 0.74/0.61).

The open-loop probe (route-following steering, fixed throttle 0.4 + AR(1) noise, scored by imagined end speed) reproduces arithmetically — 0.85/0.83/0.88 for frozen/ar03/mom_s1, my layout-bootstrap CIs [0.68,0.94]/[0.62,0.94]/[0.71,0.96]; min speed over the last 2 s 0.78/0.79/0.87 with sensitivity 0.39/0.42/0.42; en route 0.74/0.82/0.91 (CIs 0.46-1.0, 7 positives), rest 0.80/0.72/0.70 (from /tmp/decision_ctrl3.json) — but 'beats the tracker by a wide margin' is not established. (1) It is scoring-dependent: by progress the same probe gives 0.65/0.77/0.74 against the tracker's 0.65/0.71/0.69. (2) It is a between-layout signal: only 3 layouts contain both stuck and passing windows (30 pairs), and on those the probe's end speed is at chance (0.53/0.57/0.53) while the tracker by progress scores 0.70/0.77/0.73 (mine). (3) Part of it is 'the imagined vehicle reached the route end at speed within 8 s' (passing windows that terminate early end at a median 6.8-7.3 m/s); excluding early-terminated windows gives 0.82/0.67/0.78 on 45-61 windows. (4) The frozen model scores as high as the stall-trained ones, so the probe reads generic slope/state physics, not learned stall behaviour; at rest it equals the wheel-speed-excess scalar (0.78). (5) The pooled number carries the same rest/en-route inflation as every other row, and its sensitivity 0.39-0.42 equals the frozen tracker's 0.42 by min speed. It remains a deployment-fair idea worth one look, but not on the sealed arenas, which notes 13.5 declares spent.

Signal finding 1's mechanism is inverted: the variable used as 'recorded speed at the end of the seed context' was classify.json's vx_pre2s, the mean speed over the 2 s AFTER the context (the imagined window). Re-split by the true seed-state speed, the already-stationary bin (n 12) gains -2 to +2 stops over the frozen model and the still-moving > 1.5 m/s bin (n 18) gains +5 to +8. What the augmented models add is recognition of a stall already in progress: stops whose 0.8 s context already shows the vehicle rocking through zero speed (25 of 46) carry most of the gain, and within them the calls track Chrono's actual outcome (6-11 of 16 called where Chrono was stationary 4 s later, 0-1 of 9 where it was moving; frozen 4/16 vs 2/9; unchanged under AR(1) jitter). On clean forward approaches (n 7) the foresight gain is about +1 stop. Chrono itself is below 0.5 m/s at the scoring frame in only 29 of 46 stops (ceiling 0.63).

Signal finding 2 mixed two AUC definitions: 'mean 0.672 sd 0.029' and the Spearmans 0.42/0.40/0.41 are for all 271 infeasible vs feasible (frozen 0.621); on the headline stop+launch definition the 62-run mean is 0.717, sd 0.030, and the Spearmans 0.30/0.28/0.34 (the two rank runs at rho 0.90). The AR-probe stop metric correlates -0.51 with the pick (Spearman, n=22), not -0.45. 'A hard/slow-route signal, not a stall signal' overreaches: at matched commanded speed stall routes are still rejected 3-5x as often as feasible ones (wp8d_ar03 0.53 vs 0.11 at 3.5-4.5 m/s) and crawl rejections are correct on the benchmark; the supportable statement is that training raised rejection volume without sharpening the stall-vs-feasible odds ratio.

Design (a) details: '42/52 f105 at tau 0.5' is misattributed (that is the gate-fine-tune + cost-cheap-true row; the cheap predictor's own gate+fastest gives 45/52 and 46/52 on f105, 85/93 sealed); '341 infeasible = 64 contact-only + 234 stalled + 132 timeouts' are overlapping categories (sum 430); the head floor is a 5-fold-by-layout MLP, not a leave-one-layout-out logistic, and its seed-averaged values (0.59-0.73) sit slightly BELOW the cheap predictor's 0.766; 'from rest the model has no such state (AUC 0.48-0.59)' is stale (old models, old stop class) — on the corrected 46 stops the from-rest imagined speed separates at 0.78-0.89 with commanded speed at 0.71, so the from-rest trajectory carries a modest state signal beyond the route profile for the stall-trained models, though nothing puts it above the terrain predictor.

Design (b) 'already answered as parity' overreaches. On f105 (52 layouts) every paired difference between the imagination's oracle-gated cost ranking and the cheap predictor's spans zero in both directions (e.g. mom_s1 -0.06 [-0.14,+0.01], frozen +0.14 [-0.06,+0.42] at time+E/1) — underpowered, not settled. On the 93 sealed layouts (which the analyst had not re-scored) the pre-registered fine-tuned model with 60-degree limits ranks cost better than the cheap predictor at time+E/1: oracle-gate regret 1.22 vs 1.38 (true elevation) / 1.31 (predicted), paired diff -0.16 [-0.29,-0.04] / -0.10 [-0.18,-0.02], better on 34 vs 18 layouts (I re-ran /tmp/refute_b/cost_check.py); the edge is driven by the milder arena f107, absent for the frozen and scratch models (parity, +0.02/+0.00) and at the benchmark cost (1.14 vs 1.16), and cancels once infeasible picks are penalised (own-pick 1.62 vs 1.64). This is a fourth, post-hoc look at arenas the notes declare spent, so it is a motivation for a fresh mild-arena test, not a result. The feasibility drop under energy-heavy costs hits every cost minimiser (cheap 42 -> 37 on f105), not the imagination specifically.

The closing sentence of 13.11 should read: the tracker-in-the-loop 0.65-0.71 is the honest number for 'a controller trained in the frozen imagination driving the stall-trained imagination, scored by progress on windows where the stall is already under way'; it is not a measure of the imagination's stall foresight from the state, and the teacher-forced figures should be retired (a future-control scalar beats them at 0.96). Both the progress score (a vehicle rocking on the route or rolling back counts as no progress; the route end freezes it) and the pooled rest/en-route AUC should be replaced before any further decision-test number is quoted.
syn.first_experiment: Design (a) in its cheapest form, locally, with a built-in control and pre-registered endpoints, before any collection or cluster training (about 2 h of the local GPU, no Chrono, no cluster). (1) Data: re-imagine f101-f105 from rest with the WP3 tracker (scripts/traverse_wp7_imagine_cache.py, ~10 s per 722 routes) for the frozen model wp2_mapv2_pt_dag_ro8_amd (no f105 selection double-dip) and wp8e_mom_s1 (best summary-feature floor; note its checkpoint was selected on f105), dumping per-step 17-D imagined state, dead-reckoned pose (add to rollout()'s _traj in scripts/traverse_wp4_score_candidates.py) and the 256-D crop tokens (src/nedm/traverse/tracker_env.py crop()). Optional fourth arm at no extra cost: the same dump from a fixed-throttle open-loop rollout (route-following steering, throttle 0.4 + AR(1) sigma 0.0265 rho 0.3), which tests the 'closed-loop controller hides the state response' mechanism from rest. (2) Heads: one small GRU/MLP architecture, three seeds each, trained on the f101-f104 outcomes (1749 routes, 341 infeasible; early stopping by leave-one-arena-out inside f101-f104, never on f105): (i) imagined trajectory + tokens along the imagined path; (ii) the nominal route profile (commanded speed, stations, headings) + the same tokens along the nominal path with NO rollout; (iii) the existing cheap terrain-profile predictor (wp7_cheap_pred as the like-for-like camera-map control, wp7_cheap_true as the upper reference); plus commanded speed alone. (3) Endpoints on f105, written down before training: primary = AUC for stall (151 stop+launch) vs feasible (451) and for all-infeasible (271) vs feasible, with layout-cluster bootstrap CIs over the 65 layouts and a within-commanded-speed version; secondary = feasible routes rejected at the threshold that rejects 50 % of infeasible ones, and P(stall | accepted); tertiary = gate+fastest picks against the heuristic's 44/52 with the random-rejecter reference 43.9 +/- 0.7 (ceiling 8 layouts, 4 contact-only). (4) Decision rule: (i) beats (ii) by >= 0.05 AUC in all three seeds AND matches or beats (iii) -> the imagination carries information its inputs do not; proceed to fresh HARD arenas via scripts/traverse_wp8_sealed_prep.sh (difficulty 1.25; write the missing traverse_wp8_sealed_count.py; require >= 30 heuristic-failure layouts with a feasible alternative, verified model-free), one look with the head as the gate, paired sign test. (i) ~ (ii) (the expectation from the parity numbers) -> record the 'imagination as feature source' version of the thesis as closed on this family; do not spend a collection on it; design (b) only after imagined-energy fidelity on this family is restored (corr 0.5-0.65 now vs 0.9 on arena_v1) and then on a mild (difficulty < 1) fresh pair scored by regret against the refitted cheap predictor; do not build (c). (5) Land the measurement fixes alongside: fix pred_stuck at route completion in cmd_decision; score stalls by imagined |speed| rather than route progress; report the decision windows' rest and en-route strata separately with the scalar baselines (-vx at t0-1, wheel-speed excess, at-rest flag, |steer| at t0-1) and layout-cluster CIs; do not touch the sealed arenas f106/f107 again. The signal lens's 3-arena-vs-4-arena data-scaling run (four MI350 jobs, route-level endpoint) is a reasonable follow-up only if the head result is positive and more stall data are being considered; with a seed spread of 0.05 AUC against an expected effect of the same size it is underpowered as a first experiment.
syn.decision_note_for_user:
Where the stall work stands. The trained models learned to recognise a stall that is already under way, not to foresee one. The strong numbers came from information a planner would never have (the recorded driver's reactions to the stall; a single scalar of those controls outranks every model), and the honest closed-loop comparisons, once split into launch and en-route cases and given error bars, put the trained models within noise of the untrained one. On the whole-route yardstick they reject more routes but do not separate stalls from feasible routes any better in proportion. A simple terrain-profile predictor matches everything the imagination offers as a gate, and the drive-fast rule fails on too few layouts for any gate to show. Three measurement defects inflated earlier tables and should be fixed before quoting more numbers.

Recommendation: run one cheap local test (about two hours, no simulator): does a small predictor reading the imagined trajectory beat the same predictor reading only the route profile and terrain features? If not, the imagination-as-feature-source idea is closed on this terrain family and no simulator collection should go to it. The cost-side idea stays open (a modest edge appeared on the milder held-out arena, but in a post-hoc look at data already used up). Do not build the replanning design.

findings.claim: The teacher-forced AUC (0.85-0.90) is essentially all future-control leak, and part of it is not even the throttle fingerprint but the recorded steering of a stuck vehicle driving the imagined vehicle off the route. A single scalar of the recorded future controls with no state and no model, mean |delta-throttle| over the next 8 s, ranks 'stuck within 8 s' at AUC 0.96 (sensitivity 0.79 at 5 % FPR; 0.93 from the first 2 s alone), above every teacher-forced model; the future brake fraction alone gives 0.96 for run infeasibility.
findings.evidence: Computed on the 105 windows of artifacts/traverse/wp7_stall_diag/decision_verdict.json from the wp7_cache_v1 act arrays (stuck windows: |dthr| 0.013/step, brake 0.00; moving: 0.032, 0.11; throttle LEVEL at t0-1 is uninformative, AUC 0.51). Donor swap in /tmp/decision_ctrl.json: with a ladder-mate's recorded controls (same layout, same path, from its own decision point) each stall-trained model's prediction correlates 0.94-0.98 with the model's own teacher-forced prediction for the donor's window vs 0.76-0.86 with its prediction for the actual window, and on label-discordant pairs it follows the donor's label (swap_fast: own 0.00 / donor 1.00 for p6, ar03, mom_s1, n=4; swap_rand n=9: p6 0.40/0.60, ar03 0.35/0.65); the own-label AUC survives (0.82-0.87) only because ladder-mates share the label 89-95 % of the time. Steering component: in 'rec' mode 13/21/12/15 of the 33 stuck windows (frozen/p6/ar03/mom_s1) are imagined MOVING at >0.5 m/s with <3 m of route progress vs 0-3 of 72 passing windows, and the progress score counts that as a stall; scored by imagined end speed instead, teacher forcing is only 0.55/0.80/0.73/0.68.

findings.claim: The pooled 'AUC stuck within 8 s' used throughout 13.7-13.11 is inflated for every predictor by the rest/en-route stratification: 26 of the 33 positives are launch failures decided at rest (t0=16), so the flag 'at rest' alone scores 0.79 and the scalar -vx at t0-1 scores 0.82 (0.90 for run infeasibility), above the cheap context-only classifier (0.71/0.84). Honest comparisons must be within strata: 41 rest windows (26 stuck / 15 launching) and 64 en-route windows (7 stuck / 57 moving, so wide intervals).
findings.evidence: Scalar features computed from the wp7_cache_v1 z1 context at the decision windows (/tmp analysis over decision_verdict.json): -vx at t0-1 AUC 0.82 pooled but 0.57 en route and 0.66 at rest; wheel-speed excess 0.78 within the rest stratum (the perched spinning wheel); tracker-in-the-loop within strata: frozen 0.70/0.63, p6 0.74/0.61, ar03 0.68/0.60, mom_s1 0.68/0.66 (en route / rest, by progress).

findings.claim: There IS a deployment-fair control source that keeps a stall signal, untested in 13.10-13.11: an open-loop probe with route-following (pure-pursuit) steering, a fixed throttle of 0.3-0.4 plus tracker-matched AR(1) noise (sigma 0.0265, rho 0.3), scored by the imagined SPEED (not progress). It uses no recorded controls and no retraining, and it beats the tracker-in-the-loop by a wide margin: by imagined end speed, frozen 0.85, wp8d_ar03 0.83, wp8e_mom_s1 0.88 (tracker in the loop by the same score 0.54/0.44/0.54; teacher forcing 0.55/0.73/0.68); by min speed over the last 2 s 0.78/0.79/0.87 with sensitivity at 5 % FPR 0.39/0.42/0.42 (tracker 0.42/0.09/0.30). Within strata (end speed): en route 0.74/0.82/0.91, rest 0.80/0.72/0.70. The mechanism is that a closed-loop controller compensates (raises the throttle when the imagined vehicle slows) and equalises outcomes, hiding the model's own state-dependent response; the frozen model, which never learned the fingerprint, carries the signal too. The fingerprint model wp8_p6_k80_prog does not (0.55-0.63) and flips under noise (progress AUC 0.82 -> 0.48). Caveats: throttle 0.6 is less robust (ar03 0.58); holding the RECORDED control instead gives even higher progress-AUC (hold_ar 0.86/0.83/0.93/0.94) but that is partly the recorded steering, which at rest already encodes the Chrono controller's reaction (|steer| 0.43 in launch failures vs 0.25, AUC 0.75 on its own) and sends the imagined vehicle off-route, so it is not claimed as fair.
findings.evidence: /tmp/decision_ctrl3.json and .log, modes ppsteer_const4, ppsteer_const4_ar, ppsteer_const3_ar, ppsteer_const6_ar, zsteer_const4_ar; speed scores recomputed over the pre-termination part of each stored vx trace (nan-fill artefact excluded). Sweep over throttle 0.3/0.4/0.6 with noise: frozen 0.84-0.85, ar03 0.58-0.83, mom_s1 0.77-0.88 by end speed. Zero steering instead of pure pursuit: 0.77/0.78/0.63, so the route-following steering matters. /tmp/decision_ctrl2.json: fixed throttle with held recorded steering, const3/4/6, progress AUC 0.82-0.92 for all four models; hold_ppsteer (pp steering, held throttle) drops the frozen model 0.85 -> 0.65 and ar03 0.92 -> 0.71, isolating the recorded-steering contribution.

findings.claim: Design (a) — a learned stall/progress head on the imagination's own state/tokens — is the only one of the three with a cheap, local, decisive test, but its stated justification is misread and the existing evidence puts it at parity with the cheap terrain-profile predictor. What it would train: a small GRU/MLP over the from-rest tracker rollout (17-D imagined states at 20 Hz, dead-reckoned pose, 256-D crop tokens; rollout() in scripts/traverse_wp4_score_candidates.py already returns _traj z1/act, tracker_env.crop gives the tokens) on the f101-f104 outcomes (1749 routes: 341 infeasible = 64 contact-only, 234 stalled, 132 timeouts; my count from wp7_cache_v1/labels.json), selected on f105, used as gate+fastest / gate+imagined-cost in the pick table. What already answers part of it: (1) plan §32's 'the cheap classifier's 0.84 shows the state carries it' refers to a classifier reading the TRUE recorded state 5 m before the stall (wp7_stall_diag/decision_verdict.json); on those same 105 windows commanded speed alone gives AUC 0.73 for run infeasibility (my computation), the classifier's local-stuck AUC is 0.71 with sensitivity 0.00 at 5 % FPR, and the from-rest imagination has no such state (§12.2 item 6: from rest the model's predicted speed separates stops from passes at AUC 0.48-0.59). (2) What a head can read off the from-rest imagination is bounded by the rows: imagined time alone gives AUC 0.64-0.72 for infeasibility on f105 (wp8_eval/<run>/imagine_f105/summary.json), and a leave-layout-out logistic on the imagined summary features (time, log energy, max pitch/roll, min Fz, ok/completed flags, speed, length; /tmp/plan32/head_floor.py, 5 folds by layout, n=722) reaches 0.58 (frozen), 0.60 (wp7_ft_mix), 0.65 (wp8_p6_k80_prog), 0.67 (wp8d_ar03), 0.77 (wp8e_mom_s1) — at best equal to the cheap terrain-profile predictor's 0.77 on f105 (wp7_cheap_true/readout.json; 0.78 sealed, §11.5), which did not convert into picks (42/52 f105 at tau 0.5, 78/86 sealed vs the heuristic's 44/52 and 86/93). Cheapest decisive experiment (~2 h local GPU, no Chrono): re-imagine f101-f105 once with trajectories dumped, then train three heads of identical architecture and three seeds each — (i) imagined trajectory + tokens, (ii) the nominal route profile (commanded speed, stations) + the same tokens along the nominal path with NO rollout, (iii) the existing cheap predictor — and judge on f105 by AUC and by feasible routes rejected at the threshold rejecting 50 % of infeasible ones; the pick count is a secondary endpoint only. It counts as 'the imagination doing the work' only if (i) beats (ii) beyond the seed spread; otherwise the head is a terrain classifier on the frozen encoder's features. Failure modes: the head learns the terrain statistic from the tokens (most likely, given the parity above); 341 positives; f105 double-dip (checkpoint selection and readout on the same arena); contact failures (4 of the heuristic's 8 f105 failures) are invisible to a stall head.

findings.claim: Design (b) — moving the thesis to a cost-side benchmark — is already answered on the existing data and the answer is parity with a model-free predictor, not a win: re-scoring the existing f105 imagination rows under speed-penalising costs (no new runs) shows the fastest heuristic becomes beatable on cost, but the imagination's cost ranking is no better than the cheap terrain-profile regressor's, and the energy-heavy cost pushes the imagination's pick into the slow, stall-prone region so its feasibility drops. Numbers (my /tmp/plan32/cost_side.py, cost_side2.py, cost_kind.py; picks = min cost among accepted routes, fallback fastest; regret = Chrono cost of the pick / best feasible Chrono cost; 52 f105 layouts): heuristic regret 1.15 at time+E/10, 1.53 at time+E/1, 2.05 at energy-only (feasible 44/52 throughout); imagination own picks at time+E/1: regret 1.27-1.35 but feasible only 31-38/52; with an ORACLE gate (cost ranking isolated) the imagination's regret is 1.22-1.42 (time+E/1) and 1.33-1.56 (energy-only) against the cheap true-elevation predictor's 1.28 and 1.40; within-layout Spearman of energy among feasible routes: imagination 0.41-0.50 (frozen/ft_mix/p6_k80_prog/mom_s1), cheap 0.47 (true elevation) / 0.45 (predicted elevation); energy correlation on accepted feasible routes 0.51-0.65 with ratio drifting 0.81-1.26 across models, cheap 0.68 at ratio 0.99; imagined time is accurate for every model (median ratio 0.96-1.00, corr 0.82-0.91) but time is the quantity the heuristic already gets right. The §11.5 free-form 'cost win' (regret 1.11 vs 1.20, n=14) is a win over the heuristic, not over the cheap predictor (1.06 on 13 picked); on f105 free-form (n=5) cheap 1.07 vs imagination own 1.08-1.27. Where the imagination did beat a model-free scorer on cost it was on the mild arena_v1 family with energy corr 0.91-0.92 (§8), and even there the shared-bank control shrank it to -1.24 ± 0.71 on 18/33 layouts (§10.5) with the reading 'so does a regression … speed choice on gentle features is not where the world model earns its cost' (§10.7). What (b) would actually require: fresh arenas at difficulty < 1 (so slow is safe), a bank with a real time/energy trade-off, a pre-registered cost weight, a Chrono collection on newton (~1000 routes, hours) and the cheap predictor refitted as the control; no training. Note that scripts/traverse_wp8_sealed_prep.sh builds the opposite (difficulty 1.25, harder, for a stall gate), has not been run (no assets/traverse/arena_f108+, no wp8_collect_*), and its companion traverse_wp8_sealed_count.py does not exist. Failure modes: the cheap predictor matches (energy is the imagination's weakest quantity, §3, and it is what a speed penalty weighs); ride severity is not in the rows (imagined max pitch corr 0.59-0.65); the 'model-free' benchmark still has a free cost weight. It counts as the imagination doing the work (the rollout's time/energy are its output) but the advantage claim needs the cheap-predictor control, which on current evidence it does not pass.

findings.claim: Design (c) — MPC-style replanning from the live state — is already answered negatively by the decision test, and I confirmed with new runs that moving the decision point closer to or farther from the stall does not help: with the WP3 tracker in the loop the imagination's foresight of 'stuck within 8 s' on the 105 f105 decision windows is AUC 0.62/0.66/0.66/0.64 at 2 m lead (my run, /tmp/plan32/decision_lead2.log), 0.65/0.71/0.71/0.69 at 5 m (wp8_eval_summary/verdict_decision.txt) and 0.67/0.72/0.76/0.75 at 10 m (my run, /tmp/plan32/decision_lead10.log) for frozen / wp8_p6_k80_prog / wp8d_ar03 / wp8e_mom_s1, sensitivity 0.18-0.44 at 5 % false alarms; the teacher-forced numbers (0.83-0.91) are inflated by the recorded future controls (§13.11). The gate-with-tracker decision is 2-4 of 5 decidable layouts at every lead against the heuristic's 5/5 (regret 1.06), and only 5 of f105's layouts have a decision to make at the decision point at all. Every controller that can be put inside the imagination either exploits it (tracker retrained inside wp8d_ar03: AUC 0.33, pick 26-30/52; decision_wp8_tracker_ar03_s*.log, pick_wp8_tracker_ar03_s*.txt) or triggers the residual constancy cue (pure pursuit: 0.32-0.43 for the stall-trained models; decision_pure_pursuit.log). What (c) would need to build: a Chrono runner with the model in the loop on newton, camera localisation at speed, N re-imaginations per second, and fresh arenas for the endpoint — days of work for a signal that is currently absent. Its model-free confound is also the strongest on this family: one 1 m/s speed step separates stall from pass on 48 of 65 momentum layouts (§12.1), so a rule 'add throttle when slowing on a climb' would take the credit. It is the design that most fully counts as 'the imagination doing the work', which is why it must wait for a closed-loop stall signal above the frozen model's 0.65-0.67; rank last.

findings.claim: All three designs share one prerequisite the plan already named: the existing arenas have no headroom for any gate, so no pick-count endpoint on f101-f107 can be decisive. verdict.corrected_claim: Re-scoring the existing imagination rows under speed-penalising costs makes the fastest heuristic beatable on cost (f105 regret 1.53 at time+E/1 vs 1.25-1.35 for the imagination's own picks and 1.28 for the cheap true-elevation predictor), but the existing data do not settle whether the imagination's cost ranking beats a model-free terrain-profile regressor. On the 52 f105 layouts the two are indistinguishable (oracle-gate regret 1.22-1.42 vs 1.28 at time+E/1, 1.33-1.56 vs 1.40 energy-only, all paired bootstrap CIs spanning zero; matched within-layout energy Spearman 0.46-0.52 vs 0.45). On the 93 sealed layouts, which the re-scoring had not covered, the pre-registered fine-tuned model's ranking is modestly better than the cheap predictor's at time+E/1 (1.22 vs 1.38 true-elevation / 1.31 predicted-elevation; paired diff -0.16 [-0.29,-0.04] / -0.10 [-0.18,-0.02]; Spearman 0.53 vs 0.45/0.43 on 86 matched layouts) and energy-only (1.26 vs 1.35/1.36, CIs touching zero), driven by the milder arena f107, absent for the frozen and scratch models and at the benchmark cost, and cancelled once infeasible picks are penalised (own-pick penalised means 1.62 vs 1.64). The feasibility loss under energy-heavy costs hits every cost-minimising selector on this family (cheap 42 -> 37, imagination 40-42 -> 31-38 on f105), not the imagination specifically. Design (b) therefore remains open rather than answered: it needs fresh arenas at difficulty < 1, a bank with a real time/energy trade-off, a pre-registered cost weight, a Chrono collection on newton and the cheap predictor refitted as the control (traverse_wp8_sealed_prep.sh builds harder arenas at 1.25, has not been run, and its sealed_count companion does not exist); the sealed-set edge on the milder arena is the reason to run it, and the cheap-predictor control is the bar it must clear.
